messages:
lina: quick check - mobile SDK folks: is it expected that an active streaming generation gets a 401 if the app rotates the bearer token mid-stream? seeing customers hit this when background refresh happens.

ben: yep, saw that. RN fetch + EventSource paths both return 401 mid-stream. currently we just close the connection on 401. question is: should the SDK attempt a transparent reconnect+resume or surface an error?

ash: cc @ben, we decided to surface an error for streaming (short-lived streams we ask apps to reconnect). reconnect+resume needs server support for resuming KV cache + model state, too complex.

sam: agree with ash. for completions streaming we can offer a client-level helper that does reconnect+dedupe, but not automatic resume. keep it explicit.

ben: ok. actionable: document that token rotation during active stream will cause connection close with 401. also we should expose a small helper in RN SDK: .withRetry({on401: (attempt) => refreshAndReconnect})

lina: perfect. also a couple CORS edgecases from webview users: when using an embedded WKWebView on iOS we get "Access-Control-Allow-Origin" blocks for the websocket fallback. any tips?

ash: for WKWebView make sure you set the custom header via native shim not JS if you need to inject Authorization header for websockets. WKWebView blocks some headers when set from JS. we recommend ephemeral tokens in query string ONLY for webview, but warn about logs/exposure.

ben: android WebView (Chromium) is more permissive but CORS still applies for preflight. for fetch + streaming use keepalive: true for finalization pings, but note keepalive doesn't stream data.

sam: for native iOS (Swift) use URLSessionWebSocketTask for websockets. we attach token in the initial http request:

```swift
var req = URLRequest(url: url)
req.addValue("Bearer \(token)", forHTTPHeaderField: "Authorization")
let ws = URLSession.shared.webSocketTask(with: req)
ws.resume()
```

If token needs refresh while ws is open, close + reconnect.

lina: thanks. what about retry/backoff for non-streaming requests from mobile SDKs? any recommended defaults?

ash: we use jittered exponential backoff with max 5 retries for idempotent calls (embeddings, non-mutation endpoints). for generation requests consider 2 retries only because of user-perceived latency. algo: base=200ms, factor=2, jitter=uniform(0,base).

ben: adding for RN: Android OkHttp has automatic retry on network failures, but we disable it and implement our own so we can handle 429 vs 5xx differently. recommend code snippet in SDK:

```js
async function fetchWithRetry(url, opts) {
  for (let i=0;i<max;i++){
    try { return await fetch(url, opts) }
    catch(e){ await sleep(backoff(i)) }
  }
  throw new Error('max retries')
}
```

lina: good. one more: streaming + progress UI - if we reconnect, app should avoid duplicate tokens/backpressure. maybe include a unique stream-id header so server can detect duplicate reconnects?

sam: we can add X-Redwood-Stream-Id optional header. server will ignore duplicates for the last 10s but still treat as new generation (no state resume). useful for dedupe at client side. filing ticket.

ci-bot: deploy-notify: mobile-sdk v1.12.3-rc branch created for these docs changes and helper APIs (:party:).

ash: I'll submit a small PR to RN SDK: add on401 hook + docs about token rotation + example for WKWebView.

ben: sgtm. I'll add a short note in mobile quickstart about querystring tokens in webviews and security tradeoffs.

lina: thanks everyone. i'll update the devex guide and ping when PRs land. :thumbsup:
